name: Chondrodysplasia punctata, tibial-metacarpal type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Chondrodysplasia Punctata

criteria.description: Presence of punctate calcifications in epiphyseal cartilage on radiographs
Disproportionate shortening of tibiae and metacarpals
Characteristic facial features including midface hypoplasia and depressed nasal bridge
Normal peroxisomal biochemical studies differentiating from other CDP types

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of punctate epiphyseal calcifications and tibial-metacarpal shortening on radiographs
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; genetic testing may assist but is not definitive.

pathognomonic.notes: Visible on early radiographs, hallmark of the disease
searchTerms: small spots of calcium in bone ends

pathognomonic.symptomName: Disproportionate shortening of tibiae and metacarpals
searchTerms: short lower leg and hand bones
uneven shortening of leg and hand bones

pathognomonic.symptomName: Midface hypoplasia with depressed nasal bridge
searchTerms: underdeveloped middle face with flat nose bridge
sunken midface and low nasal bridge

common.notes: Growth failure evident in infancy and early childhood

common.symptomName: Joint stiffness and limited range of motion
common.notes: Due to abnormal cartilage and bone development
Radiological finding consistent with growth delay

occasional.notes: Reported in some cases but not consistent
Occasional conductive or sensorineural hearing loss

occasional.symptomName: Epiphyseal dysplasia in other long bones
occasional.notes: Additional skeletal involvement beyond tibiae and metacarpals
searchTerms: abnormal bone growth in long bones

laboratory: Normal peroxisomal function tests differentiating from rhizomelic chondrodysplasia punctata
imaging: Radiographs showing punctate calcifications in epiphyseal cartilage
Shortened tibiae and metacarpals with epiphyseal dysplasia
genetic: No consistent single gene mutation identified; diagnosis mainly clinical-radiological
other: Normal biochemical markers of peroxisomal disorders
Clinical observation of facial dysmorphism and growth retardation

distinguishingFeatures: Severe peroxisomal dysfunction with plasmalogen deficiency
Characteristic cataracts and ichthyosiform skin lesions

redFlags: Severe respiratory distress due to thoracic cage abnormalities
Failure to thrive with severe growth retardation
references: Orphanet: Chondrodysplasia punctata, tibial-metacarpal type - ORPHA:79346
Superti-Furga A, et al. Chondrodysplasia punctata: clinical and molecular aspects. Am J Med Genet C Semin Med Genet. 2013
Miller JD, et al. Radiologic features of chondrodysplasia punctata. Radiographics. 1995
